Quasar drift explorer

The Sun falls around the Milky Way, and its changing velocity tilts the light of every distant quasar a few millionths of an arcsecond per year towards the Galactic Centre. Each Gaia quasar's error is ~90 times the signal, so the pattern only appears when hundreds of thousands are averaged. Choose which quasars to use and the page refits the pattern from Gaia DR3's proper motions.

What the page computes

Gaia DR3's 1,215,942 five-parameter Gaia-CRF3 quasars, minus the 3,783 outliers of the full fit, are summed into 3,072 sky pixels (HEALPix nside 16) with their full 2×2 error weights, separately for each magnitude bin, colour bin and three random tranches (1%, 9%, 90%). The page solves the weighted least-squares fit of vector spherical harmonics up to the chosen degree (glide + rotation at l = 1, plus large-scale systematics at l = 2–3), exactly as the main analysis but with each quasar placed at its pixel's centre. Errors are the fit's errors times the unit weight error of the full fit. Arrows average all quasars within the chosen radius of each point of a coarser grid, so neighbouring arrows share quasars. By default the arrows and the profile are drawn after subtracting the fit's own non-glide terms (the frame's spin and, for lmax ≥ 2, the larger-scale patterns of Gaia's systematic errors), which are bigger than the acceleration itself; choose "raw" to see them. The profile below the map is the mean drift along (and across) the great circle through the Galactic Centre in 10° rings.
